title: Electricity Fundamentals
summary: Learn the meanings of voltage, current, resistance, and power through safe low-voltage models.
objectives: Define voltage, current, resistance, and power conceptually.
Use P = V x I in a safe, symbolic calculation without treating it as trade competency.

vocab.def: A difference in electrical potential that can drive current.
Opposition to the flow of electric charge.
A unit used to describe power.

sections.heading: Four useful quantities
sections.body: Voltage can help drive current. Resistance opposes current. Power describes a rate of energy use. A common relationship is P = V x I, where power in watts equals voltage times current.

sections.heading: Calculate in a model
sections.body: If a safe classroom model uses 5 volts and 2 amps, its conceptual power is 10 watts. This arithmetic does not authorize electrical work or prove trade competency.

sections.heading: Electrical safety is non-negotiable
sections.body: Use diagrams, simulations, or approved low-voltage kits. Never access mains panels, wire building circuits, open energized supplies, or service data-center power equipment.

practice.prompt: Use P = V x I for a 12-volt, 1.5-amp classroom model. State the result and one reason the example is not professional electrical training.

quiz.question: What does a watt describe?
options: A unit used to describe power
quiz.answer: A unit used to describe power

lab.objective: Calculate symbolic power values and interpret a low-voltage model diagram.

futureCompetencyCandidates: calculate symbolic power in a controlled exercise
reflectionPrompt: Which electrical quantity would you want explained again before a supervised low-voltage lab?
